agentConfiguration.evidence: Root reported the successful child spawn arguments. The same child continued into phase 2; no backend model-resolution metadata was exposed.

hypothesis: A small bounded owner can reuse existing prepared encounter adapters across independent lives, preserve BossBattle as the sole combat/contact update owner, and retire stale map work without introducing a second combat system or repeatedly cloning warm actor resources.

scope.productionIntegrationOwner: root: conditional lazy development actor lab only
scope.adapterOwner: B: actor definitions, existing encounter factory, resource reset and sharing

contract.factory: createAdapter(definition,{generation,isCurrent,preparation}) returns warm/reset/activate/update/hide/dispose/estimate/snapshot adapter plus existing encounter. Factory isCurrent lasts through the record's map ownership; warm/activate receive separate operation-scoped checks.
contract.spawnContext: {player,position,rotationY,mapId,spawnGroup,...adapterContext}; passed to reset and activate. Injected actual definition validator rejects player safety distance, map, navigation and occupancy before resource creation.
contract.combat: Combat adapter update is a no-op. Existing BossBattle owns encounter update/contact/input order; manager calls no combat method directly.
contract.rewards: Manager emits at most one acknowledgment per life only when adapter snapshot.rewardGranted is true; it grants no drops or quest credit. Existing adapter/battle callbacks remain the gameplay owner. Clear/recycle/map exit grant nothing.

boundsAndLifetime.capBehavior: Explicit ActorPopulationLimitError(reason); counts are never silently lowered. Reservations are synchronous before queued creation. Oversized prewarm batches roll back newly reserved records and cannot evict their own selected warm handles.
boundsAndLifetime.states: preparing -> active -> dying/corpse -> recycle -> dormant -> preparing; hidden prewarm -> dormant; cancellation -> cancelled -> disposing/disposed. Recycle is an immediate transition, not a delayed visual phase.
boundsAndLifetime.generationCancellation: Reject callers and cancel existing preparation promptly; retain the outstanding record/memory charge until its underlying creation/warm/activation settles. Release the current scheduling slot so fresh generation work can proceed within total/memory caps; eventually dispose that exact late adapter.
boundsAndLifetime.pause: update dt drives respawn and idle clocks; paused updates advance neither. No manager respawn setTimeout/interval exists.
boundsAndLifetime.respawn: One ticket per life after corpse removal. Temporary unsafe spawn retries the same ticket at a bounded cadence without moving its position or issuing another reward. Active-cap pressure retains the waiting ticket.
boundsAndLifetime.idle: Only unleased dormant records without pending respawn are eligible. Pressure evicts oldest eligible records; idle expiration uses the unpaused logical clock. Asynchronous disposal remains charged until its resource release completes.
boundsAndLifetime.memoryMeaning: Definition reservations followed by conservative adapter estimates, including declared fallback bytes; these are not measured process/GPU residency. B confirmed last-adapter refcount release for owned shared libraries and derived materials; externally injected owned:false libraries stay with their external owner. Promise-returning adapter disposal remains charged until cleanup settles.

scheduling.fullFrequency: Every active/dying/corpse adapter receives update each unpaused tick; near NPC decisions and combat/incoming/projectile/quest-relevant NPC decisions run each tick.
scheduling.farNpc: Only optional decide() calls for explicitly peaceful far NPCs are staggered. Animation/update/interact and existing combat/projectile/quest semantics are retained. Missing position information uses the full-frequency path.

integrationAsks: Use update before the existing BossBattle update and observe afterward; never update the same combat encounter twice.
Pause with the existing game/loading/settings policy and call leaveMap before map/player ownership changes.
Invoke clear without rewards from explicit UI clear and global battle reset; dispose factory-owned shared libraries after manager teardown.
Retain the normal-play lazy import gate and do not create development mass actors during ordinary play.
Complete independent actual-model 1/5/10/20, mixed, NPC, death/respawn and map-cancel scenarios before claiming phase completion.
limits: No browser automation, visual GPU validation, physical-device FPS, thermal or supported production concurrent-count claim.
The hard count 20 is a development experiment ceiling, not a promise of 20 actors at 60 FPS.
Focused manager tests use deterministic adapters; independent shipped-model verification is recorded separately.
No assets, quality/distance policy or combat-number changes were made by this owner.
